svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Glycolysis, in the cytoplasm: glucose (6C) is split and oxidised to 2 pyruvate (3C). Net 2 ATP and 2 NADH. No oxygen needed."], [4, "With oxygen, pyruvate enters the matrix. Link reaction: CO\u2082 is removed and NADH is formed, giving acetyl (2C) on coenzyme A."], [7, "Krebs cycle, in the matrix: acetyl (2C) + oxaloacetate (4C) \u2192 citrate (6C). Each turn releases 2 CO\u2082 and makes 3 NADH, 1 FADH\u2082 and 1 ATP."], [12, "Electron transport chain, on the inner membrane (cristae): NADH gives up electrons, which pass from carrier to carrier."], [13.5, "The energy released pumps H\u207a ions from the matrix into the intermembrane space, building a high H\u207a concentration there."], [16, "Oxygen is the final electron acceptor: it combines with electrons and H\u207a to form water."], [17, "Chemiosmosis: H\u207a flow back through ATP synthase, which turns and makes ATP from ADP + Pi. Most of the ATP from respiration (about 30 per glucose) is made here."]]
svg.title: Mitochondrion and aerobic respiration
svg.desc: A mitochondrion with outer and inner membranes, cristae, matrix, ribosomes and DNA, with glycolysis in the cytoplasm, the link reaction and Krebs cycle in the matrix, and an inset of the electron transport chain and ATP synthase.
svg.text: Mitochondrion drawn as in an electron micrograph (about 1–3 µm long). Inset: a strip of inner membrane, much enlarged.

g.data-info: Glycolysis happens here, outside the mitochondrion, and does not need oxygen.
Smooth outer phospholipid bilayer. Pyruvate passes through it into the mitochondrion.
Narrow space between the membranes. H⁺ ions are pumped into it, so its H⁺ concentration becomes high (low pH).
Fluid inside the inner membrane: the link reaction and the Krebs cycle happen here, using its enzymes.
Holds the electron transport chain and ATP synthase. It is impermeable to H⁺ except through ATP synthase.
Folds of the inner membrane: a large surface area for many electron transport chains and ATP synthase molecules.
Small, like bacterial ribosomes (evidence for endosymbiosis): make some mitochondrial proteins.
Naked, circular DNA, like a bacterium’s (evidence for endosymbiosis).
Acetyl (2C) joins oxaloacetate (4C) to form citrate (6C). Each turn: 2 CO₂, 3 NADH, 1 FADH₂ and 1 ATP; oxaloacetate is regenerated.
In the matrix: pyruvate (3C) is decarboxylated (CO₂ lost) and oxidised (NADH formed), giving acetyl (2C), carried by coenzyme A.
Glucose (6C) is phosphorylated, then split and oxidised to 2 pyruvate (3C). Net gain: 2 ATP and 2 NADH.
Holds the electron transport chain and ATP synthase. It is impermeable to H⁺ except through ATP synthase.
Protein complexes in the inner membrane. Electrons from NADH and FADH₂ pass along them, releasing energy used to pump H⁺ into the intermembrane space.
H⁺ ions flow back down their gradient through ATP synthase (chemiosmosis); this turns part of the enzyme and makes ATP from ADP + Pi.
Oxygen accepts the electrons at the end of the chain and combines with H⁺ to form water. Without oxygen the chain stops.
